newsitem.title: japan: TIFFE euroyen ends up, Dec loses benchmark status.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends up, Dec loses benchmark status.

text.p: The key three-month December Euroyen futures contract ended firmer on Monday as sentiment was moderately bullish on the expectation the Bank of Japan's quarterly corporate sentiment survey due on Wednesday would show Japan's economic recovery was stalling once again.
The December, of which turnover has fallen behind that of March for two consecutive days, will lose its benchmark status from the night session on Monday, a TIFFE official said.
The new benchmark March ended the day session at 98.87, compared with the Friday settlement of 98.85.
The BOJ's survey, known as the tankan, will be released at 8.50 a.m. on Wednesday (2350 GMT Tuesday).
Forecasts by economists polled by Reuters ranged from minus four to plus four for the June diffusion index (DI) for major manufacturers, and from minus three to minus 10 for major non-manufacturers.
Traders said the market is unlikely to move much, if the major manufacturers' DI is in a range of minus four to plus one.
The majority of the market expects the tankan to provide evidence that Japan's economic recovery is again stalling.

But any signs of an improvement in corporate sentiment, such as a major manufacturers September DI of beyond plus two, would rattle the euroyen market which has mostly priced in weak tankan results, traders said.
The market is also interested in a prospective coupon set on the new 10-year JGB to be offered on Tuesday.
If the new 10-year JGB bears a low 2.5 percent coupon, that would induce hedge selling in the JGB futures market, which in turn, could depress the TIFFE euroyen, traders said.

In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, a relatively large amount of payment in three and five-year fixed interest rates by a few Japanese banks was detected, but the operations were not conducted in a manner to influence rates, IRS traders said.
The three year IRS was quoted at 1.52/1.56 percent at 0656 GMT, compared with 1.53/1.57 percent on Friday.
The five year IRS was quoted at 2.07/11 percent, unchanged from Friday.
